findings.obs_text: In Neh 13:13 duty (H5921A) stands two words after considered: the treasurers were counted reliable, and their duty follows, to distribute to their brothers. WordNet relates the subgroup to this collection through respect; the verse pairs counting with duty.
In Jos 7:21 hidden (H2934) stands six words after the weighing of the gold bar, at the end of Achan's account: what he weighed in his telling he also hid.
findings.grounds: they are hidden in the earth

older.finding: *Ṭāman*, "to hide, bury". A thing is put into or under something. Achan's plunder is "hidden in the earth inside my tent" (Joshua 7:21). Moses "hid him in the sand" (Exodus 2:12). An enemy's net is hidden in the path (Psalm 140:5). It is also the word for the sluggard who "buries his hand in the dish and will not even bring it back to his mouth" (Proverbs 19:24).
older.reason: a word study of the hiding words (taman): it states what the words mean and where; the conceal collection owns it

older.finding: Hiding what I hold: A person can hide what he has done. Achan tells it in order: "when I saw … then I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the earth inside my tent" (Joshua 7:21). Joshua had to ask him first: "do not hide it from me" (7:19).; What happens next differs.
older.reason: it states how conceal works in a person; the conceal collection owns it

The seat is the victim's life or spirit | Objects hidden (Gen 35:4; Jos 2:6; Jer 13; 43). Two notes: Jos 7:21 has coveting (M18) followed by hiding, and Pro 19:24 / 26:15, "the sluggard buries his hand in the dish", shows
older.reason: a word study of the hiding words (taman): it states what the words mean and where; the conceal collection owns it

older.finding: (a) Concealing one's own wrong. Each case has its own sequence: Achan: "when I saw … then I coveted them and took them. And see, they are hidden in the earth inside my tent" (Jos 7:21); Joshua: "tell me now what you have done; do not hide it from me" (7:19); Achan: "Truly I have sinned" (7:20); "behold, it was hidden in his tent" (7:22); Seeing, coveting, taking, hiding, being demanded to disclose
older.reason: it states how conceal works in a person; the conceal collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Col 2:16 judgment on (G2919) stands eight words before with regard to: no one is to judge them in the matters the link names.
findings.grounds: let no one pass judgment on you

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:117 continually (H8548) stands two words after regard and qualifies it: the speaker asks to have regard for the statutes without end.
findings.grounds: have regard for your statutes continually

findings.obs_text: In Isa 53:8 transgression (H6588) stands eight words after considered, in what the generation did not consider: the one cut off was stricken for the transgression of the people.
findings.grounds: for the transgression of my people

findings.obs_text: In Deu 9:27 wickedness (H7562, with H2088 and H0413 at the same place) stands three words after regard as what God is asked not to regard: the stubbornness, wickedness and sin of the people.
findings.grounds: Do not regard the stubbornness of this people

findings.obs_text: In Pro 12:10 cruel (H0394) stands five words after regard, on the other side of the contrast: the righteous regard the life of their beast, the mercy of the wicked is cruel.
findings.grounds: the mercy of the wicked is cruel

older.finding: Wickedness is here the wickedness, ungodliness or sinfulness of a person as a state or practice of the heart, set against godliness and what is right (ungodliness, a heart busy with iniquity, a wicked deed, sinful passions).
older.reason: it states a face or use of the cruel words; the cruel collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Exo 5:9 lying (H8267) stands directly after regard as its object: the men are to pay no regard to lying words.
findings.grounds: pay no regard to lying words

findings.obs_text: In 2Ch 5:11 consecrated (H6942G) stands two words before regard: every priest present was set apart, and the regard that is set aside is for the divisions of their service.
In Eze 18:28 committed (H6213H) stands six words after considered, in what the man considered: the transgressions he had committed, from which he turned away.

older.finding: Consecrated is here the act of consecrating oneself or one's heart to the Lord: a purposeful act of the person's will, dedicated to God.
older.reason: it states a face or use of the dedicate words; the dedicate collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Isa 13:17 delight (H2654A) stands three words after regard, in the parallel line: no regard for silver, no delight in gold.
In Lam 4:16 favor (H2603A) stands seven words after regard, in the parallel lines: the Lord regards them no more, and no favor is shown to the elders.
In Act 28:22 desire (G0515) stands seven words before with regard to: the leaders desire to hear Paul's views, and the link names the sect spoken against.
findings.grounds: we desire to hear from you

findings.obs_text: In Job 2:3 destroy (H1104) stands eighteen words after considered, at the end of the Lord's words: Satan incited him to destroy Job without reason.
In Psa 74:20 violence (H2555) stands seven words after regard, in the reason the covenant is to be regarded: the dark places are full of violence.

findings.obs_text: In Job 1:8 and Job 2:3 evil (H7451B) stands twelve and thirteen words after considered, in the description of the one considered: he turns away from evil.
In Pro 12:10 wicked (H7563) stands four words after regard, on the other side of the contrast with the righteous who regard.

older.finding: Wicked is here the godly, the righteous, the upright, the wicked or the ungodly as a class of persons toward whom an act is directed or whom an event befalls (the Lord keeps the godly, do not envy the wicked, Christ died for the ungodly); the act is named by another word of the verse.
